title: From a Goat's Dance to Two Billion Cups: How Coffee Crossed the World
title_zh: 从山羊的舞蹈到二十亿只杯子：咖啡如何走遍世界
intro_zh: 本文约525词，含6个四级核心词（legend / cultivate / empire / luxury / ban / resist），句子难度中等（3/5），理解目标85%-90%，分8段，配有4道四级阅读理解选择题。

paragraphs.en: Every morning, some two billion cups of coffee are drunk around the world. For many of us, the drink is simply part of the day. Yet a thousand years ago, the small red cherries that hold the coffee bean grew wild on the cool hills of Ethiopia, and almost nobody outside Africa had ever tasted them. The story of how they travelled the globe is full of surprises.
paragraphs.zh: 每天早晨，全世界大约要喝掉二十亿杯咖啡。对我们许多人来说，这杯饮料不过是日常的一部分。然而在一千年前，包裹着咖啡豆的小小红果还只是野生地长在埃塞俄比亚凉爽的山坡上，非洲以外几乎没有人尝过它。关于它如何走遍全球的故事，充满了意外。

paragraphs.en: An old legend tells of Kaldi, a young goat herder in the ninth century. One afternoon he noticed that his animals were jumping and running after eating berries from a certain tree. Curious, Kaldi tried the fruit himself and soon felt awake and cheerful. He carried some to the monks at a nearby monastery. The monks found that the drink helped them stay awake during long night prayers, and word of the plant began to travel.
paragraphs.zh: 一则古老的传说讲到九世纪一位年轻的牧羊人卡尔迪。一天下午，他发现羊群吃了某种树上的果实后，又是蹦又是跑。出于好奇，卡尔迪自己也尝了尝，很快就觉得清醒又愉快。他摘了一些带给附近修道院的修士们。修士们发现这种饮料能帮他们在漫长的夜间祈祷中保持清醒，关于这种植物的消息便开始传开了。

paragraphs.en: By the fifteenth century, people in Yemen, at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, had learned to cultivate the plant. Instead of eating the fruit, they roasted and ground the seeds, then poured hot water over them — close to the coffee we know. The port of Mocha became famous, and its name is still used for a coffee-and-chocolate drink today.
paragraphs.zh: 到十五世纪，位于阿拉伯半岛南端的也门人已经学会了种植这种植物。他们不再吃果实，而是把种子烘烤、研磨，然后浇上热水——这已经接近我们今天所喝的咖啡了。摩卡港因此声名远扬，直到今天，一种咖啡加巧克力的饮品仍沿用这个名字。

paragraphs.en: Coffee houses soon appeared in cities such as Mecca and Cairo. Men gathered there to play chess, listen to music, discuss news and argue about politics. Because so much information moved through these rooms, people called them 'Schools of the Wise.' A traveller from Europe wrote that in these places you could learn more in an hour than in a month of ordinary conversation.
paragraphs.zh: 很快，麦加、开罗等城市里出现了咖啡馆。人们聚在那里下棋、听音乐、谈论新闻、争论政治。由于大量信息在这些房间里流转，人们把它们称作“智者学校”。一位来自欧洲的旅行者写道，在这些地方待上一小时学到的东西，比平时闲聊一个月还多。

paragraphs.en: When the Ottoman Empire expanded, the drink went with it. In 1554 the first coffee house opened in Constantinople, and by 1615 Venetian traders had brought beans to Italy. London followed in 1652. Within fifty years the city had hundreds of coffee houses, and Oxford students nicknamed theirs 'penny universities' — for the price of a cup, you could join a table of merchants, scientists and writers.
paragraphs.zh: 随着奥斯曼帝国的扩张，这种饮料也随之一路传播。1554年，君士坦丁堡开设了第一家咖啡馆；到1615年，威尼斯商人已把咖啡豆带到了意大利。伦敦在1652年紧随其后。五十年间，这座城市就有了数百家咖啡馆，牛津的学生给自家附近的咖啡馆起了个绰号叫“一便士大学”——只要一杯咖啡的钱，你就能和商人、科学家、作家同桌而坐。

paragraphs.en: Not everyone was pleased. At first coffee was a luxury only the rich could afford, and some rulers saw the crowded coffee houses as dangerous places where people might share ideas against the government. In 1675 King Charles II of England tried to ban them; the public resisted so strongly that he gave up within days. Other cities in Europe and the Middle East ordered coffee houses closed, yet the drink kept spreading.
paragraphs.zh: 并非所有人都乐意。起初咖啡是只有富人才买得起的奢侈品，而一些统治者把挤满人的咖啡馆视为危险之地，认为人们会在那里交流反对政府的想法。1675年，英国国王查理二世试图禁掉咖啡馆；公众的抵制如此强烈，他几天之内就放弃了。欧洲和中东的其他城市也曾下令关闭咖啡馆，但这种饮料仍在继续传播。

paragraphs.en: European companies then took coffee farming overseas. The Dutch planted it on Java in the 1690s. Around 1720 a French naval officer, Gabriel de Clieu, carried a single seedling across the Atlantic to Martinique; within sixty years the island held millions of trees. Seeds reached Brazil in 1727, and that country is now the largest producer on Earth.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，欧洲的贸易公司把咖啡种植带到了海外。荷兰人于17世纪90年代在爪哇岛种植咖啡。约1720年，法国海军军官加布里埃尔·德·克利厄把一株幼苗带过大西洋，送到马提尼克岛；六十年内，这座岛上就有了数百万棵咖啡树。咖啡种子于1727年传入巴西，而巴西如今是全球最大的咖啡生产国。

paragraphs.en: Today coffee is grown in more than fifty countries and employs millions of small farmers, most of them on small family plots. Prices rise and fall, and a warming climate is pushing good growing land uphill. Next time you hold a warm cup, remember: a dancing goat, a monk's night prayer and one brave seedling on a ship all helped to make this ordinary drink.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，五十多个国家种植咖啡，数以百万计的小农户以此为生，其中多数人耕种的是家庭小地块。咖啡价格时涨时落，而气候变暖正把适宜种植的土地推向更高的山坡。下次你捧起一杯热咖啡时，不妨想想：一只跳舞的山羊、一位修士的夜间祈祷，以及船上的一株勇敢幼苗，共同造就了这杯寻常的饮料。

questions.q: According to the old legend, what made Kaldi try the coffee berries?
options: A monk gave him the fruit as a gift.
He saw his goats jumping and running after eating them.
He was searching for a way to stay warm at night.
He found the berries floating in a river.
questions.explain: 细节题。第二段明确说卡尔迪注意到羊群吃了树上的果实后“又是蹦又是跑”，出于好奇他自己也尝了，故选B。

questions.q: Why did Oxford students call their coffee house a 'penny university'?
options: The university paid for all their coffee.
A cup cost about a penny, and they could learn from the people at the table.
Only students who owned one penny were allowed in.
It was built right next to the university.
questions.explain: 细节兼理解题。第五段说“for the price of a cup, you could join a table of merchants, scientists and writers”，即花一杯咖啡的钱就能和商人、科学家、作家同坐交流，如同上大学，故选B。

questions.q: What can be inferred about King Charles II's attempt to ban coffee houses?
options: It was warmly supported by the public.
It successfully lasted for many years.
It failed because people opposed it strongly.
It was copied by every city in Europe.
questions.explain: 推断题。第六段说公众“resisted so strongly that he gave up within days”，几天内就被迫放弃，说明禁令因公众强烈反对而失败，故选C。

questions.q: The word 'cultivate' in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。第三段讲也门人学会“cultivate the plant”，紧接着说他们烘烤研磨种子、冲泡饮用，说明此词指人工栽种，与grow最接近，故选A。
